summary.headline: Venus Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR320.5 crore and EBITDA hit a record INR51.5 crore, with margin flat at 16.1%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR320.5 crore, up 16% YoY, with management calling it the highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA. EBITDA rose 14.7% to INR51.5 crore, but margin of 16.1% was broadly flat versus 16.2%, and PAT grew 6.5% to INR26.4 crore. Domestic revenue grew 31% to INR227 crore, while exports fell to INR94 crore from INR103 crore on geopolitical disruption. Fittings, value-added seamless and welded capacity started in May 2026, and the data-centre spooling line (about INR70 crore capex, INR185 crore LOI) is targeted for end-2026 commissioning.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR103 crore in Q1 FY26
vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26, broadly flat

financial_highlights.value: More than INR600 crore (excl. INR185 crore spooling LOI)
financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR450 crore last quarter per analyst

segments.name: Seamless pipes & tubes
segments.commentary: Revenue 55% of mix, up 15% YoY; utilisation around 85-90% (one answer said ~90%), with new capacity commissioned end-May 2026.

segments.name: Welded pipes & tubes
segments.commentary: Revenue 39% of mix, up 21% YoY; utilisation around 60%, with value-added tubing started in FY26.

segments.name: Fittings
segments.commentary: Commercial production started May 2026; management expects 5-7% of FY27 revenue and 8-10% in FY28, though approvals are still in progress.

segments.name: Spooling (data-centre SFN)
segments.commentary: Planned capex about INR70 crore backed by INR185 crore LOI; commissioning targeted end of Q3 FY27, with management guiding about 5% of FY27 and 10-15% of FY28 top line.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20%, with seamless and welded each around 20%; management said volume growth above 15% and it was maintained.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected below 17%; management targets about 18% in the next two years, with margin inching up from Q2 FY27 onward.
Capex of about INR100 crore in FY27: about INR70 crore spooling, some fittings and machinery, about INR15 crore maintenance and a solar plant.
Export share intended to stay above 30%; export order book is more than 40-45% of the INR600 crore order book.
Management said revenue could double by around FY29-FY30, with a verbal reference to INR2,500 crore before that point; this was not formally guided.
capex_capacity: Seamless capacity added at the end of May 2026; utilisation expected to rise each quarter, with a target of more than 80-85% for seamless and more than 60-65% for welded in FY27-28.
Fittings and value-added seamless and welded capacity commenced in May 2026.
Spooling facility (about INR70 crore capex) targeted to start end of Q3 FY27, with major portion of data-centre capex targeted before December 2026.
Management said spooling output should be at least 3x asset turn in revenue.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand healthy across oil & gas, chemical, pharma, engineering and power; order inflow mix includes repeat power customers and new engineering/chemical customers.
Export order inflow strong from the US; export revenue dipped on geopolitical disruption, with Q2 pickup intended but container and geopolitical issues flagged.
Realisations rose with steel prices, and EBITDA per kg improved.
Management said competition exists but is not undercutting in pipes; new entrants in spooling were noted.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation levels and is the ~20% growth guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Welded utilisation about 60%, seamless about 85-90%; FY27 growth guidance maintained at a similar level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order book rise about INR150 crore in a quarter, and from which sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly power, engineering, chemical and oil & gas; the order book stood above INR600 crore, plus the INR185 crore spooling LOI.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 margin outlook and FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 margin below 17%; target about 18% over the next two years, with fittings and spooling contributing from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR325 crore at June 30, 2026; FY27 capex about INR100 crore, of which INR70 crore spooling.

qa_highlights.question: Why did data-centre revenue expectations move up versus the earlier spooling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects part of the capex to overlap Q4 FY27, with the major portion done before December 2026 and execution through December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EU safeguard quota not the cause of the export decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to geopolitical factors; the EU quota was cut 25%, and India has historically exceeded the quota.

risks_watch: Export decline (INR94 crore vs INR103 crore) from geopolitical and container disruption; the Q2 recovery is uncertain.
Fittings approvals and spooling customer qualification may take months, so the ramp-up timeline is uncertain.
Margin flat at 16.1% YoY despite the record EBITDA; the path to 18% depends on value-added mix and utilisation.
Net debt of about INR325 crore and working-capital borrowings are a concern, raised by an analyst on interest costs versus depreciation.
Inconsistency on the spooling revenue timeline: INR37 crore run-rate vs ~INR70 crore FY27 target versus Q4 commissioning.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term margin and order-book expansion, but cautious on exports and the timing of fittings and spooling approvals. Several answers were loose on numbers (e.g., the net debt figure was corrected mid-answer and utilisation was quoted in different ranges), and management declined to share volume and realisation splits.
key_quotes: Overall, we believe Venus is entering an important phase of its growth journey.
But definitely for FY27, it should be less than 17% on an overall basis.
Competition is there, but not as such like undercutting.

adds.what: Fittings and value-added seamless and welded capacity

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% is maintained, backed by seamless capacity added end-May 2026, a more than INR600 crore order book (excluding INR185 crore spooling LOI), and the INR70 crore spooling facility targeted for end-Q3 FY27; FY27 EBITDA margin guided below 17%.
